title: Prism - a side project of a side project, for tracking AI limits and PC stats
author: todastar
selftext:
I work full-time and build things on the side: games, an ERP, and little tools that I find useful. I also experiment with different AI apps and models rather than sticking to just one.

I like ChatGPT for brainstorming. I use Codex too, although managing its remaining allowance can get tricky. Cursor’s cloud coding has been useful when I’ve planned the work properly, and OpenCode has been an inexpensive way for me to try different models, including Chinese ones. I’ve also used Opus and Sonnet quite a bit for coding.

At some point, I wanted a simple answer to: how much usage do I have left across these tools?

That’s how Prism happened. Basically, a side project of a side project. Maybe lot of other users have created something similar or simpler. But this one has been helping me alot.

It’s a Windows desktop widget that keeps the reported remaining allowance from supported accounts in view. It currently has connections for Codex, Cursor Individual, OpenCode Go and Claude, plus optional OpenRouter key-credit tracking. It refreshes periodically, so there’s a little lag. It’s showing provider-reported allowance, not an exact count of tokens left.

The system stats came from another problem. Some of my Codex runs went on for a couple of days, with Node processes running builds and checks. Sometimes the CPU and RAM usage got high enough to make my laptop crawl. I wanted to see that happening too, so I added system vitals alongside the AI readings.

You can choose what appears, keep it compact, or use a narrow ribbon near the taskbar. There’s also quota history, low-allowance alerts and reminders for known resets.

I built this with help from GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol. It’s been useful to me, so I thought I’d put it out there for anyone else juggling a similar setup.

It’s free and MIT-licensed. Feel free to download it, use it, fork it, or tell me what looks wrong or could be better. Feedback on the readings, setup and overall layout would be especially helpful.

[https://github.com/kumarnabh/prism-widget](https://github.com/kumarnabh/prism-widget)

Setup note: Windows 10/11 x64 and Python 3.11–3.14 are required. Windows 11 is the locally tested platform, and the release binaries are unsigned. Installation details are in the README.
